findings.evidence: The candidate selects the first ancestry-path commit as the Wave projection, then checks git rev-parse <projection>^ against the approved Wave commit. For a merge, ^ resolves only the first parent. Reachable merge c9260e1e981fea84a651dd59104aad12e1fb8d8e has parents 8a4d8be and 25f4fe4 while <merge>^ returns only 8a4d8be, proving a second parent can inject approval or slice-projection state while the purported direct-child check passes. This leaves GOV-MAINT-0010.R02-F03 only partially closed.
findings.remediation: Select the projection on the proposal's first-parent authority chain, obtain its complete parent list with git rev-list --parents -n 1, require that list to equal exactly [approved_wave_commit], and add a real-Git multi-parent projection-injection rejection fixture.
